name: Tools
author: Tor Erik Ottinsen

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga forum, AMOS Factory downloads section, retrieved 2026-07-26. Most items there are credited "provided and archived by Lonewolf10". Archive path: Tools_1.01.
provenance.note: Documentation coverage was measured by counting how many of the library's own keyword names appear in the files shipped beside it, taking only files that can be documentation (not disk images, example programs or the library itself). That measures the DOCUMENTATION, which is what the `docs` field records; it does not set the evidence tier, which follows from what is available to read.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified unless stated in the notes. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: PORTED, 33/33 keywords faithful; see src/runtime/tools.ts. Tor Erik Ottinsen's personal toolbox, made public -- "originally developed for personal use only. As time passed it grew as I needed more commands". A byte array in a memory bank, a cursor you point at memory and then read and write through, a Range, an Encode/Decode pair, a checksum, and eleven `Oui` keywords the author declined to describe: "internal commands of no use for anybody except me. I therefore choose to leave them undocumented." Read from the 2,164-byte hunk (50 jump-table entries, 33 of them keywords) with AMOSPro_Tools.Guide covering the other twenty-two and giving every argument order; the eleven are the binary alone, and `Oui Init` turned out to describe the whole shape -- (N+1) records of 32 bytes, with the bank's first two bytes holding a count and a maximum, fourteen words of fields, a live flag at +$1a and a string pointer at +$1c. Two defects and several NOTES. `Array Dim SX,SY` stores SX+1 as the stride and MULTIPLIES X BY IT, so the array is really indexed [0..SY][0..SX] -- the dimensions are the other way round from the guide's own `Dim _ARRAY(SX,SY)` and from AMOS's, and it only stays inside the allocation while SX <= SY; nothing bounds-checks anything, and the index is a word displacement that wraps negative at 32768. `Oui New` never increments the count, so successive calls all write element 1 -- deliberate rather than missed, since `Oui Set Data 0,n` is exactly the byte it lives in and the count reads as a cursor the caller drives. `Set Crypt` is one instruction, `eori.b #$ff`, with the length word left in clear; `Encode`/`Decode` are a genuine stream cipher with a 15-bit LCG and a position-dependent running sum. `range` is slot-qualified because Range 2.6/2.9Plus claims the name too, which the guide itself half-admits: "a somewhat optimized version of the Range command in the Shuffle Extension". One DEVIATION: `Oui Reserve Text` parks a pointer to AMOS's TEMPORARY string workspace in the bank, which the next string expression reclaims, so on the machine an element's text survives only until then; strings have no addresses here, so the buffer comes from a pool of its own and the pointer is stable -- the one place this port is kinder than the library.
